system: S1 ML-QEM (Liao et al., Nature Machine Intelligence 6, 1478-1486, 2024)
scoped_experiment: 4-qubit TFIM Trotter on ibm_algiers hardware; RF over tabular circuit features; target = noiseless Z expectation value on each of 4 spins

declared_before_fitting.source: phase1/RUN-RECORD-S1.json, written before any arm existed
declared_before_fitting.loss: per-row L2 distance between predicted and ideal 4-vector, averaged over rows (the system's own metric, h36 cell 51)
declared_before_fitting.resample_unit: one test row (one circuit execution on ibm_algiers, evaluated on all 4 observables jointly)
declared_before_fitting.interval: 95% pointwise percentile, S formed inside each draw

arms.A: LinearRegression per observable on descriptor columns 0..164
arms.C: RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=0) per observable on descriptor columns 0..164
arms.F_refitted: RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=0) per observable on all columns 0..168
arms.F_released: docs/paper_figures/hardware_over_depth.pk df['rfr_list'], the table that produced the published figure

DECLARED_READING.why_not_split: encode_data_v2_ecr builds vec = [] (mlp.py:157) and its X[:, vec_slice] assignment (mlp.py:170) is commented out; feature width is exactly 5 + 160 + 4 = 169. The scoped experiment's released data directory holds only the circuit batches, results.pk, results_unshuffled.pk and index_order.json, with no backend-properties artifact, and h36 imports get_backend_properties_v1 without ever calling it.

leakfree_qualification.status: qualification; the declared number is the all-rows one

saturation.verdict: HIGH: the released descriptors carry substantial information about the target, so this is not a low-saturation case

released_vs_refitted_F.note: reported, not reconciled; the plan forbids adjusting the recipe after seeing this gap

leak_check_4.verdict: FIRES, recorded and reported per the plan, not aborted
leak_check_4.direction: favours the descriptor arms, therefore favours a PRESENT reading

qualifications.1_leak4: 277 of 2500 test rows (11.1%) share a descriptor block with a training row, all 250 step-0 rows plus 27 step-1 rows. It favours the descriptor arms and therefore favours a PRESENT reading. On the 2223 leak-free rows with the declared arms, S = 0.5534 [0.5348, 0.5730], still PRESENT.

2_weak_affine_arm.spec: OLS on 165 descriptor columns, 500 training rows
2_weak_affine_arm.verdict: overfitting, not degenerate: it fits the training rows and generalizes poorly
2_weak_affine_arm.why_it_matters: S = (A-C)/(A-F) increases with A, so a weak affine arm pushes S toward 1

4_joint_stress.what: the strongest affine arm (RidgeCV, cross-validated on training rows only) applied to the leak-free rows
4_joint_stress.meaning: the declared PRESENT reading is robust to each qualification on its own but not to both together

5_affine_ceiling_sweep.meaning: on the declared evaluation set every affine arm in the sweep reads PRESENT; on the leak-free subset the reading depends on which affine arm is used

scripts: phase2_verify.py       re-verifies the phase-1 handoff and re-runs all four leak checks
phase2_score.py        builds A, C, F; both calibration rungs; T, K, D, S inside each draw
phase2_appendix.py     affine-arm weakness, trivial baselines, capacity-match check
phase2_stress.py       joint stress of the two qualifications
phase2_affine_ceiling.py  bounds how far a stronger affine arm can move S
debug_identity.py      isolates the n_jobs=-1 float-summation nondeterminism
